title: Introduction to Financial Accounting
description: Provides an introduction to financial accounting concepts. Introduces students to the rules for recording financial transactions under the U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP). Illustrates how to build core financial statements from transactions and how to combine information from the various financial statements to analyze firm performance.

title: Introduction to Managerial Accounting
description: Introduces the use of accounting information for management purposes, including decision-making, planning, and control of operations. Students learn to integrate topics in cost determination, economic analysis, budgeting, and management and financial control.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT 2301.

title: Intermediate Accounting I
description: An overview of financial statements and revenue recognition that focuses on the left-hand side (assets) of the balance sheet. Provides the necessary foundation for comprehension by users and preparers of the information in financial statements.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT 2302. Restricted to Cox majors and Pre-MSA 4+1 student group.

title: Intermediate Accounting II
description: Continuation of ACCT 3311. Focuses on items on the right-hand side (liabilities and stockholders’ equity) of the balance sheet.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT 3311. Restricted to Cox majors and Pre-MSA 4+1 student group.

title: Intermediate Financial Reporting
description: This accelerated course provides a rigorous and fast-paced exploration of financial reporting principles, focusing on their role in financial statement analysis. It covers key accounting topics such as revenue recognition, asset and liability measurement, equity transactions, and financial statement presentation, with an emphasis on how accounting choices influence reported financial performance. Through real-world financial statements, case studies, and data-driven exercises, students examine the impact of accounting decisions on businesses and markets. The course is designed for those seeking a deeper understanding of financial reporting in preparation for careers in finance and business analysis. Accounting majors take ACCT 3311/ACCT 3312 and cannot receive credit for the course.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ACCT 2301 and ACCT 2302. Restricted to Cox Majors.

title: Accelerated Intermediate Accounting for Analysis
description: This accelerated course provides a rigorous and fast-paced exploration of financial reporting principles, focusing on their role in financial statement analysis. It covers key accounting topics such as revenue recognition, asset and liability measurement, equity transactions, and financial statement presentation, with an emphasis on how accounting choices influence reported financial performance. Through real-world financial statements, case studies, and data-driven exercises, students examine the impact of accounting decisions on businesses and markets. The course is designed for those seeking a deeper understanding of financial reporting in preparation for careers in finance and business analysis. Accounting majors take ACCT 3311/ACCT 3312 and cannot receive credit for the course.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ACCT 2301 and ACCT 2302. Restricted to Cox Majors.

title: Accounting Information Systems
description: Covers understanding, developing, and analyzing financial and management computerized accounting systems used by professionals in all areas of accounting and the technology that applies to them. Examines the flow of information in a computerized accounting system and explores the interaction of the different components of the enterprise with the information system. Students learn how to document, design, and operate a system that reaches far beyond the boundaries of the general ledger.
prerequisites: Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Data Analytics for Accounting
description: Introduces advanced quantitative modeling techniques for business decision-making. Covers a variety of modeling techniques, business analytics concepts, and data analysis tools. Students learn to implement these techniques in spreadsheet models that assist businesses in understanding and managing risk and improving decision-making. Applications cover a broad range of functional areas, including operations, accounting, finance, marketing, and human resource management.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ACCT 2302, ITOM 2308, ITOM 3306, and FINA 3320. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Cost Accounting
description: Focuses on the measurement, accumulation, and control of costs. Topics include product cost accounting, cost behavior analysis, direct costing, standard cost variance analysis, and relevant cost analysis.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT 2302. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Auditing and Assurance Services
description: Studies the theory and practice of auditing and other assurance services. Provides a foundation of concepts and methods that enable auditors to express an opinion on management assertions related to their client’s financial statements and other business information. Auditing standards at the national level are stressed. Ethics, internal control, government regulation, and audit reporting are other topics emphasized, as well as the behavioral characteristics and mechanics of accounting fraud.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT 3311. Restricted to Cox majors and Pre-MSA 4+1 student group.

title: Federal Income Tax
description: Covers the conceptual basis and structure for the determination of income taxes, including the tax research methods used in preparing tax returns, solving problems, and planning business decisions.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT 3311. Restricted to Cox majors and Pre-MSA 4+1 student group.

title: Accounting Theory
description: Study of selected topics and current issues in the area of accounting theory.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT 3312. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Independent Studies in Accounting
description: Directed research in accounting.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ACCT 3311, junior standing, and instructor approval.

title: Accounting Internship
description: Prerequisites: Senior standing and departmental approval.

title: Accounting Internship
description: Prerequisites: Senior standing and departmental approval.

title: Accounting Information Systems
description: Covers understanding, developing, and analyzing financial and management computerized accounting systems used by professionals in all areas of accounting and the technology that applies to them. Examines the flow of information in a computerized accounting system and explores the interaction of the different components of the enterprise with the information system. Students learn how to document, design, and operate a system that reaches far beyond the boundaries of the general ledger.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT 3311. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Advanced Financial Accounting
description: Addresses advanced accounting topics that fall into four general categories of specialized and complex aspects of accounting and financial reporting: accounting for intercorporate transactions and in particular, mergers and acquisitions; translation and remeasurement of foreign currency subsidiary statements; accounting for derivative instruments; and accounting for governmental and not-for-profit entities. Understanding of these topics is critical for preparers and users as they can materially affect practically every financial statement line item.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ACCT 3311 and ACCT 3312. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Special Topics: International Business Administration
description: Offered through SMU Abroad.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior standing. Restricted to Cox majors and minors in business fall 2021 and beyond, and minors in business with energy management fall 2024 and beyond.

title: Directed Study
description: Directed research in business.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior standing and permission of the instructor.

title: Directed Study
description: Directed research in business.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ACCT 2312, junior standing, and permission of the instructor.

title: Business Internship
description: Offered study abroad only.

title: Advanced Studies in Risk Management
description: Students work with the professor on individualized research projects targeting risk management and insurance topics.

title: Directed Study
description: Directed research in business.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ACCT 2312, junior standing, and permission of the instructor.

title: Special Topics: International Business Law
description: Special topics in international business law taught abroad.
prerequisites: Restricted to Cox majors and minors in business fall 2021 and beyond, and minors in business with energy management fall 2024 and beyond.
department: Real Estate, Risk Management & Business Law

title: Business Law
description: A study of the legal environment governing business entities, operations, and relationships to provide a legal foundation for careers in business. Topics may include introduction to the US and comparative legal systems, dispute resolution, torts, contracts, ecommerce and data privacy, business entities and governance, employment law, administrative law, intellectual property, securities law, international business, and business acquisitions.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: BLI 1110 and BLI 1210. Restricted to Cox majors.
department: Real Estate, Risk Management & Business Law

title: Business Discovery
description: Introduces various business topics, including an overview of business disciplines and careers in those fields as well as the development of skills for effective career management.
prerequisites: Restricted to students in the BBA Scholars and Business Direct Program.

title: Business Communications
description: Improves students' professional success by becoming more effective communicators. Improves presentation skills and business writing; enhances ability to plan and manage projects in a team setting; increases understanding of contemporary business communication issues; increases appreciation for the vital role that communication plays in leading a successful business. Students complete BLI 1210 during their first year at SMU, or in their second year if admitted via the internal or external transfer process.
prerequisites: Restricted to BBA Scholars, Business Direct students, and students admitted to Cox through the internal or external transfer process.

title: Life Cycle Economics: Personal Financial Planning for Today and Tomorrow
description: Students focus on personal life cycle economics as the foundation for personal financial planning in a “hands-on” classroom environment. Typical topics include how to make optimal personal finance decisions and plan for the future, based on the ideas of Nobel prize winners. The best living standard, human capital estimation, investments, and retirement planning are woven with day- to- day topics like credit scoring, taxes, personal insurance, and Social Security benefits. Analysis undertaken with commercial financial planning software. Students must bring a laptop that runs Microsoft Excel to each class. Open to all SMU students. For Cox majors this course counts as free elective credit only.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Sophomore standing.

title: Perspectives on American Business Through the Lens of General Motors
description: Examines the interactions among technological change, business strategy, government regulation, and society using the automobile industry as a unifying lens. Through historical and contemporary cases, students analyze product and process innovations; labor relations; environmental impact; mobility services; and emerging technologies such as electric, autonomous, and flying vehicles. The course emphasizes managerial decision making in complex institutional environments and develops students’ ability to evaluate the societal consequences of business and technological choices.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ECO 1311. Restricted to Cox majors and minors in business.

title: Evolution of American Capitalism
description: Discusses the evolution of capitalism in the American economy from the Colonial Period to the present. Topics include the evolution of women in the workforce, the economic situation for minorities in America, structural changes and the disappearance of the middle class, the growing income gap between rich and poor, the growth of government, the drift towards socialism, the intense competition among states for jobs and challenges to America's leadership in the global economy.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ECO 1311, ECO 1312. Restricted to Cox majors and minors in business fall 2021 and beyond, and minors in business with energy management fall 2024 and beyond.

title: Markets and Freedom
description: Discusses the indicators of economic freedom and the benefits of globalization. Explores how markets raise living standards, including the roles that technology, globalization, public policy, and economic growth play in a functioning market economy.
prerequisites: Restricted to Cox majors.

title: From Prospect to Production to Kilowatts: The Business of Energy
description: Provides an in-depth understanding of the petroleum, natural gas, coal, power generation, and alternative fuels market segments, with a focus on structure, key business drivers, and technologies. Recommended foundational course for students pursuing careers in energy, energy finance, or sustainability related disciplines.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Sophomore status and above. Restricted to Cox majors and minors in business with energy management fall 2024 and beyond.

title: The Business of Energy: Power Generation, Renewables and Sustainability
description: Provides an in-depth understanding of the power generation and renewable market segments, with a focus on long-term environmental and sustainability issues such as carbon management, land use and impact, energy poverty, and other issues developing within the sector. Provides an overview of the economics, technologies, and sustainability impacts associated with the ongoing energy transition. Recommended second course for students pursuing careers in energy, energy finance, or sustainability related disciplines.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Sophomore status and above. Restricted to Cox majors and minors in business with energy management fall 2024 and beyond.

title: Environmental Strategy for the Energy Sector
description: Equips future energy leaders with a practical understanding of environmental and sustainability challenges facing the energy sector. Students explore how engineering and scientific principles, social frameworks, and economic theory intersect to inform responsible decision-making in energy organizations. Key topics include environmental impact and risk assessment and feasibility studies tailored to energy systems. The course emphasizes interdisciplinary thinking and strategic analysis.

title: Energy Private Equity Practicum
description: Students work with a professor(s) and an industry sponsor – energy company, private equity firm, or other investment vehicle - to evaluate an energy investment opportunity and/or develop a strategic plan for the sponsor. Student may work on valuation, due diligence, risk management, market survey, or other analysis as required by the client. Application required.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: BUSE 3331. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Active Management of Energy Portfolio
description: Offers practical experience in energy and sustainability investments in public markets through management of the Spindletop Investment Fund. Analysis of macroeconomic forces and energy sector, and determining how the analysis affects investment decisions. Topics include tactical asset allocation, security selection, valuation analysis, development of a portfolio strategy, and presentation skills to a professional audience. By application.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Senior standing.

title: Energy and Environmental Law
description: Examines the legal and regulatory issues applicable to energy as they relate to finance, investment, and the economics of the business. Provides the basic tools of an energy professional to identify and analyze the legal and regulatory issues related to energy and resource development and operation, property acquisition and divestiture, and project valuation and financing. Reserved for Cox majors.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: BUSE 3331.

title: Business Management, Planning, and Analysis in Energy
description: Through energy industry case studies, examines modern operational, economic, and financial aspects of the modern energy industry as they relate to planning and decision-making in the firm, with particular emphasis on oil and gas and power generation. Topics include the energy transition, capital structure, reserve valuation, political risk, environmental risk, and sustainability. Reserved for Cox majors.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: BUSE 3331.

title: Global Energy Markets, Business, and Policy: Spikes, Myths, and Risks
description: Examines the interrelationship among the economics of global energy markets, business profitability, and public policy as it relates to the energy business. Topics include the principles of exhaustible resource economics and their impact upon business decision-making, the impact of price shocks on the industry and the overall economy, and the global policy and regulatory environment faced by the industry.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: BUSE 3331 or permission of instructor. Restricted to Cox majors or by permission of instructor.

title: Introduction to Entrepreneurship and Innovation
description: Provides a broad overview of entrepreneurship and innovation as a driver of economic and social value. Explores the fundamentals of entrepreneurship, including identifying opportunities; developing business models; and understanding the startup process; as well as the psychological, ethical, and leadership dimensions of entrepreneurial success.
prerequisites: Restricted to Cox majors and BUSNS minors.

title: From Creative Insights to Impact
description: Topics in this course include the nature of creative insight; the development of an innovative mind-set in individuals; the antecedents, processes, and barriers to individual and team creativity; and the development of the skills essential to the stimulation and creation of entrepreneurial opportunities.
prerequisites: Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Entrepreneurial Law and IP Strategies
description: Students apply practical legal tools and strategies to real-world situations commonly faced by startups and emerging ventures. Through the lens of a selected startup concept, students explore topics such as founders’ agreements, fundraising, global expansion, and exit strategies. Emphasis is placed on intellectual property—its protection, monetization, and use as a strategic asset in new venture growth.
prerequisites: Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Entrepreneurship: Starting a Business
description: Covers planning for a new business. Topics include the personal characteristics of entrepreneurs, profit and cash flow forecasts, sources of information, sales forecasts and the importance of relevant experience, entrepreneurial marketing, financing, and the business plan.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: FINA 3320, ITOM 2308, MKTG 3340 or ADV 1341, MATH 1309 or MATH 1337, and MNO 3370. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Managing the Entrepreneurial Business
description: Explores the unique challenges and opportunities involved in the management and ownership of a closely held enterprise. Examines key business, personal, and interpersonal issues relevant to the continuity and management of these firms. Topics include strategic management and corporate governance, life cycle and systems analyses, and leadership.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MNO 3370. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Topics in International Finance
description: Offered through SMU Abroad.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior standing. Restricted to Cox majors and minors in business fall 2021 and beyond, and minors in business with energy management fall 2024 and beyond.

title: Financial Management
description: Survey of concepts, practices, and problems surrounding financial markets, securities, and decision-making. Includes time value of money, market efficiency, evaluation of securities, and capital budgeting.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ACCT 2301; ECO 1311 and ECO 1312; one from the following: CS 4340, OREM 3340, STAT 2331, STAT 4340. Restricted to Cox majors and minors in business fall 2021 and beyond, and minors in business with energy management fall 2024 and beyond.

title: Advanced Corporate Finance Lab
description: Involves hands-on modeling of finance problems, including valuation for capital budgeting, public and private companies, integrated cash flow models, and exposure to handling large financial databases. Must be taken concurrently with FINA 4325.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: FINA 3320; MATH 1309 or MATH 1337. Corequisite: FINA 4325. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Quantitative Financial Modeling Lab
description: Involves hands-on advanced financial modeling, exposure to Bloomberg terminals and handling large financial databases, and advanced topics in using market and portfolio data. Must be taken concurrently with FINA 4326.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: FINA 3320; MATH 1309 or MATH 1337. Prerequisites or corequisites: FINA 4325 and FINA 4125. Corequisite: FINA 4326. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Quantitative Trading and Strategies
description: Covers a number of issues and quantitative trading strategies most often used in the hedge fund management arena. Focuses on standard hedge fund strategies like long/short equity and convertible arbitrage, and hedge fund strategies that exhibit asymmetric risk, fixed-income arbitrage, commodity investing, commodity trading advisors, and macro fund strategies. Covers the measurement of hedge fund returns for the purpose of putting together a hedge fund of funds from an analytical perspective. Application required.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: MATH 1309 or MATH 1337; FINA 4325, FINA 4125, FINA 4326, and FINA 4126. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Special Topics in Energy Finance
description: Provides students with detailed knowledge of valuation methods, project finance, risk management practices, geopolitical risks, and institutional players in the energy industry. Topics vary from term to term. Application required.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MATH 1309 or MATH 1337. Prerequisites or corequisites: FINA 4325, FINA 4125. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Independent Study
description: Directed research in finance.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: FINA 3320, junior standing, and permission of the instructor.

title: Advanced Corporate Finance
description: In-depth analysis of capital budgeting, cost of capital, sources of capital open to the firm, capital structure, dividend policy, mergers, and bankruptcy. Must be taken concurrently with FINA 4125.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: FINA 3320. Corequisite: FINA 4125. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Investment Analysis and Portfolio Management
description: Evaluates the risk and return of individual assets (US stocks and fixed-income securities), analyzes the interrelationships of risky assets when combined in portfolios, and also studies asset pricing theories, factor models, and the implications of such. Must be taken concurrently with FINA 4126.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: FINA 3320. Prerequisites or corequisites: FINA 4325 and FINA 4125. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Derivatives
description: Introduces analysis of financial derivatives such as futures, swaps, and options. Covers the underlying theories explaining derivatives markets and discusses strategies such as hedging and arbitrage.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: FINA 4325 and FINA 4125, FINA 4326 and FINA 4126. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: International Finance
description: Examines international financial markets and such issues as interest rate differences between countries’ spot and forward transactions in international currencies, and the impact of international operations for the corporate financial manager.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: FINA 4125, FINA 4325, FINA 4126, and FINA 4326. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Advanced Concepts in Financial Management
description: Selected advanced topics in corporate finance. Varies as to when offered, and what topics are covered.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: FINA 4325, FINA 4125, FINA 4326, FINA 4126.

title: Practicum in Asset and Wealth Management
description: Offers practical experience in investments through management of the Ann Rife Cox Investment Fund. Economic and industry analysis and determining how that analysis affects investment decisions. Topics include money and capital market forecasts, selection of individual securities, development of a portfolio strategy, and additional topics in asset and wealth management. By application.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: FINA 4325, FINA 4125, FINA 4326, FINA 4126.

title: Markets and Financial Intermediation
description: Analyzes the structural interrelationships among the important participants in the U.S. financial markets and the management of financial institutions. Topics include flows of funds, determinants of interest rates, monetary policy and interest rates, money and capital market instruments, commercial banks and other lending institutions, regulation of financial institutions, and risk management in financial institutions.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: FINA 4325 and FINA 4125. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Financial Statement Analysis for Valuation
description: Discusses financial statements, building on prerequisite accounting classes, but taking the perspective of a financial decision maker rather than a producer of financial statements. Students gain the knowledge and skills required by a financial analyst focused on valuation and other financial decisions. Students understand financial statement analysis, earnings quality, forecasting, valuation, and related topics.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: FINA 3320; and ACCT 3311 or ACCT 3415. Prerequisites or corequisites: FINA 4325 and FINA 4125. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Alternative Assets
description: Focuses on leveraged finance and the necessary skills to calculate total enterprise valuation. Also, the different segments of leveraged finance: high-yield bonds, leveraged loans, credit default swaps, collateralized debt obligation, debtor-in-possession financing, and distressed investing. Application required.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: FINA 3320 and ACCT 3415. Prerequisites or corequisites: FINA 4347, FINA 4325, and FINA 4125. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Information Systems for Management
description: Discusses information technology and information resources for business. Builds spreadsheet proficiencies focusing on the use of spreadsheets for business data analysis and reporting. Introduces database concepts along with tools and skills required to explore, analyze, extract, aggregate and report data.
prerequisites: Restricted to Cox majors only.

title: International Topics in Information Technology and Operations Management
description: Offered through SMU Abroad.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior standing. Restricted to Cox majors and minors in business fall 2021 and beyond, and minors in business with energy management fall 2024 and beyond.

title: Operations Management
description: Introduces concepts, principles, problems, and practices of operations management, and discusses methods for building business analytics models to solve operational business problems effectively. Topics include decision analysis, optimization (particularly linear programming) and sensitivity analysis, time-series analysis and forecasting, inventory control, simulation, and project scheduling.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ACCT 2301; ECO 1311 and ECO 1312; ITOM 2308; MATH 1309 or MATH 1337; and one from the following: CS 4340, OREM 3340, STAT 2331, STAT 4340. Restricted to Cox majors only.

title: Software Tools for Business Analytics
description: Covers the essentials of computer programming and enables students to gain proficiency in structured programming in Python; basic data management, including acquisition, storage, and access to real world data; Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA); and programming of decision models. Learn data visualization methods and various open-source packages, and how to build insights and communicate these insights through stories.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ITOM 2308. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Data Management for Business
description: Covers fundamental issues in database creation and design, including conceptual modeling, logical and physical design, data definition languages, and data manipulation languages like SQL. Covers methods for data capture, data extraction from databases, and the design of data-based applications to answer business questions related to the database. Homework assignments and an implementation project reinforce both the design issues and the practical skills covered in the course. Requires a PC that can run Windows applications.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ITOM 2308 and ITOM 3355. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Supply Chain Management
description: Covers the supply chain from the perspective of a general manager. Students learn how supply chain design and planning decisions impact the performance of the firm as well as the entire supply chain. Each class session is a blend of theory presentation and case discussion, during which some spreadsheet modeling and analysis may be required.

title: Business Intelligence
description: Starts with the design and use of enterprise data management systems for management decision support, such as data warehouses and data marts, multidimensional databases, and OLAP. Provides hands-on experience with data warehouses and related peripheral systems, as well as data management skills that are essential for successful business analytics in large and medium-size traditional enterprises. Covers Hadoop and Spark, the platforms at the heart of most big data analytics initiatives. Heavy emphasis on the development of skills required for students to be successful as analysts.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ITOM 2308. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Business Modeling with Spreadsheets
description: Introduces advanced quantitative modeling techniques for business decision-making. Covers a variety of modeling techniques, business analytics concepts, and data analysis tools. Students learn to implement these techniques in spreadsheet models that assist businesses in understanding and managing risk and improving decision-making. Applications cover a broad range of functional areas, including operations, accounting, finance, marketing, and human resource management.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ACCT 2302, ITOM 2308, and ITOM 3306. Restricted to Cox majors..

title: Supply Chain and Logistics Management
description: Covers the supply chain and logistics management from the perspective of a business analyst. Analyze the entire flow of information, materials, and services from suppliers through factories and warehouses to the end customer. Involves application of quantitative optimization and descriptive models to support supply chain and operations management decisions, using spreadsheets and other software. Students learn how supply chain design and planning decisions impact the performance of the firm as well as the entire supply chain. Reserved for Cox majors.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ITOM 3306 and ITOM 4307.

title: Business Analytics and Supply Chain Management Practicum
description: A project course that enables students to understand the complexities of a complete BASM project and the major components of the system development life cycle (SDLC) and agile analytics development. Students work with real companies to understand their business analytics challenges, and using real data, apply the academic concepts, including the analysis of the business needs which they have learned in the classroom, to build a solution for the company.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ITOM 2308, ITOM 3355, ITOM 3360, ITOM 4307 and ITOM 4320. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Predictive Analytics and Machine Learning
description: Covers various methods for gaining insights from both structured and unstructured business data. Starts with discussion of time series forecasting, then covers machine learning and data mining technologies, such as neural networks, clustering, and association-based reasoning, and examines how companies can apply these technologies to different types of decision and planning problems. Also covers AI/ML applications in various functional areas, such as training, customer service, process improvement, and operations.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ITOM 2308 and ITOM 3306. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Business
description: Explores the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in modern business environments, with a focus on its applications in operations, marketing, and finance. Students gain a strategic understanding of how generative AI and agentic AI are applied, reshaping industries, enhancing decision-making, and driving innovation. Through real-world case studies and hands-on exercises, students learn to apply these models in class, developing actionable insights into leveraging these technologies for competitive advantage.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ITOM 2308. Restricted to Cox majors only.

title: Business Intelligence and Big Data
description: Starts with the design and use of enterprise data management systems for management decision support, such as data warehouses and data marts, multidimensional databases, and OLAP. Provides hands-on experience with data warehouses and related peripheral systems, as well as data management skills that are essential for successful business analytics in large and medium-size traditional enterprises. Covers Hadoop and Spark, the platforms at the heart of most big data analytics initiatives. Heavy emphasis on the development of skills required for students to be successful as analysts.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ITOM 2308. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Project Management Analytics
description: Equips students with advanced quantitative tools to optimize project performance, enhance decision-making, and mitigate risk. Through a combination of lectures, case studies, and hands-on experiential learning, this course covers tools and concepts that enable project managers to evaluate, manage, and execute critical functions of any project while ensuring speed, efficiency, and market impact. It also covers data-driven approaches to evaluating and prioritizing projects based on strategic alignment, resource availability, and risk assessment.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ITOM 2308 and ITOM 3306. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Topics in International Marketing
description: Offered through SMU Abroad.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior standing. Restricted to Cox majors and minors in business fall 2021 and beyond, and minors in business with energy management fall 2024 and beyond.

title: Fundamentals of Marketing
description: Examines the nature of marketing decisions; the environment in which these decisions are made; and the relationship of these decisions to the firm, business, and society. Students may not receive credit for both MKTG 3340 and ADV 1341.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Restricted to Cox majors, minors in business fall 2021 and beyond, minors in business with energy management fall 2024 and beyond, BBA Scholars or Business Direct entering SMU fall 2020 and beyond, or CXMN intent to declare the minor in business.

title: Marketing Research
description: Explores the role of information in marketing decisions, discusses research methods, and teaches students how to plan and execute a research project. Reserved for Cox majors.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MKTG 3340 or ADV 1341.

title: Consumer Behavior
description: Helps students understand the motivation and behavior of buyers and consumers. Discusses consumer behavior within a marketing framework and relates it to marketing management.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MKTG 3340 or ADV 1341. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Sales and Distribution Management
description: A multidisciplinary approach to the study of sales and sales force management. Focuses on the total sales process: selection, training, motivation, and compensation of personnel; sales forecasting; sales territory management; and analysis. Provides a fundamental understanding of the elements of the sales process and a management perspective to plan, organize, and direct a sales force.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MKTG 3340 or ADV 1341. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Retailing
description: Examines the strategic role of retailing in the distribution of consumer goods and services. Students learn why consumer insight and superior execution are critical factors for building retail brands that will be successful in the future. Key topics include retail formats, multi-channel retailing, retail market strategy, merchandise assortment, supply chain, store layout and design, customer buying behavior, customer relationship management (CRM), retail pricing, and retail communication mix.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MKTG 3340 or ADV 1341. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: International Marketing
description: Examines international marketing from the underlying common nature of all humans in the global arena to the subtle nuances of localized marketing strategies in the subregions of international markets. Emphasizes novel problem-solving and an expanded worldview, with a focus on real-world approaches to understanding the global marketing environment. Reserved for Cox majors.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MKTG 3340 or ADV 1341.

title: Product and Brand Management
description: Deals with the management of product development programs and the appraisal of the many factors that affect product decision-making. Examines policies concerning branding, product line strategy, and compliance with social and government restrictions.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MKTG 3340 or ADV 1341. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Digital and Social Media Marketing
description: Explains the most important digital marketing concepts and provides hands-on experience with relevant digital channels. Examines what it takes to conceive, plan, and execute a digital campaign. Explores social media and emerging digital marketing trends. Topics include online ads, content marketing, mobile marketing, search engine marketing, and social media.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MKTG 3340 or ADV 1341. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Customer Engagement and Experience
description: Explores concepts and tools including customer journey mapping, rewards/loyalty programs, digital and social media, metrics, personalization using AI and machine learning, and customer research. Students work in teams to conduct a customer engagement and customer experience strategic audit of a company. Through lectures, guest speakers who discuss best practices, and the audit project, students learn how to engage customers with personalized interactions across all touchpoints.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MKTG 3340 or ADV 1341. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Luxury Marketing
description: Focuses on strategies and practices specific to the luxury goods and services market. Students examine consumer behavior, unique marketing approaches required to build and sustain a luxury brand, and current trends in the global luxury industry.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MKTG 3340 or ADV 1341. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Marketing Management
description: Provides a fundamental understanding of the marketing strategy planning process within the firm and develops skills for coping with the marketing management problems encountered by senior marketing managers, general management executives, and marketing consultants. This capstone course for marketing majors includes case analysis, class projects, and/or marketing simulation. Reserved for senior marketing majors.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: MKTG 3340 or ADV 1341.

title: Honors Marketing Project
description: Designed to help students develop their own research project, from the initial idea to presentation of the key findings. Includes identifying interesting research questions, designing and implementing surveys, analyzing data, documenting procedures, and communicating results. The class is highly interactive and consists of lectures, discussions, workshops, and short student presentations. Reserved for Cox majors.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: By application only.

title: Managerial Problem Solving and Decision-Making
description: Provides students with a better understanding of the process of managerial problem solving and decision-making. Students learn how to identify and analyze problems, evaluate potential solutions, and make effective decisions in a variety of organizational contexts. The course also covers decision-making biases and traps, the role of intuition and creativity in decision-making, and the importance of communication in the decision-making process. Throughout the course, students engage with case studies and experiential exercises that allow them to practice the problem-solving and decision-making skills they are learning. They also develop critical thinking skills and learn to apply analytical techniques to real-world situations. By the end of the course, students are equipped with the tools and knowledge necessary to make more effective decisions and solve complex problems in a managerial context.
prerequisites: Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Special Topics in International Management I
description: Offered through SMU Abroad.
prerequisites: Restricted to Cox majors and minors in business fall 2021 and beyond, and minors in business with energy management fall 2024 and beyond.

title: Special Topics in International Management II
description: Offered through SMU Abroad.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior standing.

title: Management
description: Develops skills in managerial behavior that facilitate high performance and satisfaction as well as continued self-development for all organization members.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Restricted to Cox majors, minors in business fall 2021 and beyond, minors in business with energy management fall 2024 and beyond, BBA Scholars or Business Direct entering SMU fall 2020 and beyond, or CXMN intent to declare the minor in business.

title: Human Capital and Talent Management
description: A thought-provoking study of how companies manage and deploy their people assets. Students learn to become more effective people managers, examining the various techniques, strategies, and practices used by companies and managers to leverage their human capital. The content also ensures students are better equipped for their professional employment journeys, arming them with actionable insights on recruiting practices, compensation philosophies, and other practical business skills. Reserved for Cox majors.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MNO 3370.

title: Negotiations
description: Presents theories and processes of negotiation as practiced in a variety of settings. Focuses on understanding the behavior of individuals, groups, and organizations in the context of competitive situations. Emphasizes simulations, role-playing, and cases. Reserved for Cox majors.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MNO 3370.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Ethical Leadership
description: Develops managerial decision-making and stakeholder analysis through a study of ethical dilemmas in contemporary business. Topics include whistle blowing, corruption, bribery, human rights, crisis management, role of corporate boards, lobbying, philanthropy, externalities, and sustainability.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MNO 3370. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Design Thinking for Organizations
description: Focuses on the principles and practices of design thinking as applied to organizations, their employees, and their clients. Students learn how to apply a design approach that prioritizes the needs, experiences, and perspectives of the people who are impacted by change, and in the process create more effective, human-centered organizations. The course covers topics such as user research, prototyping, and iterative design, as well as the role of empathy and inclusion in design. Students have the opportunity to practice applying the principles of human-centered design to the types of challenges faced by many real-world organizations. By the end of the course, students are equipped with the basic skills that are needed to identify and implement changes within organizations that are not only efficient and effective but also based on evidence.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MNO 3370. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Management Consulting and Organizational Change
description: Covers the fundamentals of management consulting, including the consulting process, client engagement, and ethics in consulting. Students learn how to identify opportunities for improvement, articulate and communicate organizational problems, and implement effective change initiatives. The course also teaches students how to navigate the consultant-client relationship and uphold the ethical and professional responsibilities of consultants. Throughout the course, students are given opportunities to apply what they are learning and develop their own consulting skills. They also learn to evaluate the effectiveness of consulting interventions, and navigate the unexpected challenges that often arise. By the end of the course, students should be equipped with the essential knowledge and skills necessary to become effective consultants and change agents in a variety of organizational contexts.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MNO 3370. Restricted to Cox Majors.

title: Pandemics! The Science of Disease Spread, Prevention, and Control
description: Explores the science of epidemic and pandemic prevention, treatment, and control, and examines what we’ve learned from pandemics across time, ranging from the bubonic plague to COVID 19.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Instructor consent required.

title: Global and Public Health Impact
description: An interdisciplinary approach to creating sustainable impact in global, public, and population health. Taught through engaging discussions, case studies, and by helping local health organizations solve difficult institutional and community challenges.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Instructor consent required.

title: Project Management: The Managerial Process
description: Presents a set of practices and interpersonal skills designed to deliver business results that are on time and on budget and meet quality standards. Examines project management in modern industries and organizational structures as a preferred, standard process to achieve successful results. Discusses defining the project goals, developing a plan to achieve the goals, executing the plan, and evaluating progress. Covers interpersonal skills, including communication, collaboration, and team management.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MNO 3370. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Leadership and Culture
description: Enhances effectiveness and success as a leader. Emphasizes core theories of motivation, leadership, interpersonal relationships, culture, and communication.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MNO 3370.

title: Leadership and Culture in the Southwest
description: Study of the psychological, behavioral economics, sociological, and organizational behavior foundations of leadership within the context of the human diversity factors of gender, ethnicity, and culture. (SMU-in-Taos)
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MNO 3370. Restricted to Cox majors.

title: Organizational and Workforce Analytics
description: Equips students with analytical skills to understand and address complex business problems by using employee data, scientific methods, and sophisticated analyses. Possible topics covered include descriptive analytics (e.g., data visualization, query, data slicing), predictive analytics (e.g., forecasting, classification, simulation), and prescriptive analytics (e.g., optimization); all using real life contexts and datasets in areas such a talent development, retention, and program evaluation. Students also have exposure to techniques for linking metrics to business strategies and organizational performance to maximally leverage a firm's human capital for sustained competitive advantage.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ITOM 2308 and MNO 3370. Restricted to Cox Majors.

title: Independent Studies in Organizational Behavior I
description: Considers contemporary issues (theoretical, ethical, methodological, social, etc.) that are currently of interest to organizational theorists and behavioral scientists. Reserved for Cox majors.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MNO 3370.

title: Topics in International Real Estate
description: Offered through SMU Abroad.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior standing. Restricted to Cox majors and minors in business fall 2021 and beyond, and minors in business with energy management fall 2024 and beyond.
department: Real Estate, Risk Management & Business Law

title: Real Estate Fundamentals
description: Introduces various aspects of the real estate property and capital markets, including market analysis, financing, investment, and legal principles. Serves as the foundation for other courses in real estate. Reserved for Cox majors.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ACCT 2302 and FINA 3320.
department: Real Estate, Risk Management & Business Law

title: Real Estate Practicum
description: A real estate industry-focused experiential learning opportunity that prepares students for careers in commercial real estate. The backbone of the course is the management of the SMU Real Estate Impact Investment Fund, a discretionary, student-managed, open-ended “evergreen” investment fund that targets direct equity investments in a variety of real estate projects in communities where the investment will create a demonstrable impact. Students learn all aspects of real estate private equity investing, including fundraising, originating and sourcing transactions, asset management, project capitalization, and dispositions. Students work in groups and are responsible for preparing investment memoranda and presenting prospective investments to the fund’s Investment Committee for approval. This course requires significant out-of-class work and enrollment in the spring term course RE 4221. Course enrollment is by application. Instructor consent required.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: RE 3381. Restricted to Cox majors.
department: Real Estate, Risk Management & Business Law

title: Real Estate Practicum
description: A real estate industry-focused experiential learning opportunity to prepare students for careers in commercial real estate. The backbone of the course is the management of the SMU Real Estate Impact Investment Fund, a discretionary, student-managed, open-ended “evergreen” investment fund that targets direct equity investments in a variety of real estate projects in communities where the investment will create a demonstrable impact. Course enrollment is by application. Students learn all aspects of real estate private equity investing, including fundraising, originating and sourcing transactions, asset management, project capitalization and dispositions. Students work in groups and are responsible for preparing investment memoranda and presenting prospective investments to the fund’s Investment Committee for approval. Requires significant out-of-class work. Instructor consent required.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: RE 4220. Restricted to Cox majors.
department: Real Estate, Risk Management & Business Law

title: Real Estate Market Analysis and Strategy
description: Explores fundamental questions faced by institutional investors in commercial real estate. Uses a data-driven and leading indicators approach to implementing the fundamental models/concepts of urban economics. Students undertake in-depth analysis of real estate cycles, examine how such insights are implemented, learn how city and property characteristics impact the decision to invest at a specific point in the cycle, explore the factors that shape the built environment and impact value, and learn about common preferred property-specific attributes.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: RE 3381. Restricted to Cox majors.
department: Real Estate, Risk Management & Business Law

title: Real Estate Law
description: An in-depth study of legal principles and documents as they relate to the real estate industry. Classes include an overview of real estate, real estate principles, the judicial system, and real estate markets. Specific classes focus on understanding and documentation of various real estate transactions and legal issues in specific industry areas such as sales and acquisitions, leasing, finance, environmental, land use, water law, agency and brokerage, and regulation. Reserved for Cox majors.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: RE 3381.
department: Real Estate, Risk Management & Business Law

title: Real Estate Markets and Valuation
description: Presents principles and techniques of estimating the value of residential and income producing properties. Considers the economic base and distribution of land use in urban areas. Includes case studies involving the cost and income approaches to valuation of real estate properties. RE 3381 may be taken concurrently with the permission of the instructor and the department chair.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: RE 3381 and FINA 3320. Restricted to Cox majors.
department: Real Estate, Risk Management & Business Law
repeatability: RE 3381 may be taken concurrently with the permission of the instructor and the department chair.

title: Real Estate Finance
description: Focuses on preparing students for careers in commercial real estate by developing the more advanced analytical and financial skills necessary to be successful in today’s diverse real estate industry. In addition to covering both acquired and developed real estate investments, the course covers both debt and equity capital structures as well as funds, including the various valuation methodologies utilized to arrive at investment decisions. Students evaluate a variety of product types through the lens of various market participants to arrive at risk adjusted investment decisions spanning core to opportunistic returns. Topics also cover structured debt such as mezzanine loans and preferred equity. Students create financial models in Excel on both an unlevered and levered basis. Proformas also include various sensitivity analyses, as well as partnership and fund waterfalls. To support investment underwriting, students are also required to conduct independent research to analyze market data. In addition to independent work, course requirements include a variety of group case studies.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: FINA 3320 and RE 3381. Restricted to Cox majors.
department: Real Estate, Risk Management & Business Law

title: Real Estate Capital Markets
description: Focuses on the analysis and valuation of Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and Commercial Mortgage Backed Securities (CMBS). REITs and CMBS are the largest class of traded equity and debt securities linked to commercial real estate and also the most informationally transparent part of the real estate capital markets.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: RE 4389. Restricted to Cox majors.
department: Real Estate, Risk Management & Business Law

title: Strategic Management in a Global Economy
description: Analyzes the processes of building competitive advantage and strategy execution in single- and multi-business firms, with emphasis on industry evolution, the boundaries of the firm, and global competition.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ACCT 2301; ACCT 2302; FINA 3320; ITOM 2308; one of the following: CS 4340, OREM 3340, STAT 2301, STAT 2331, STAT 4340; MATH 1309 or MATH 1337; MKTG 3340 or ADV 1341; and MNO 3370. Restricted to Cox majors.
